Switchboard is the closest structural near-miss to Strale found during the Phase 3 Session 2 broadened search. The structural distance is product-shaped rather than strategy-shaped, which means it could close inside a single release window. Re-checking at every strategic review cycle is how the near-miss stays a near-miss instead of becoming a competitor we did not see coming.

Three structural distance criteria to check each cycle:

1. Does Switchboard run independent continuous testing of data against ground truth on a published schedule (not just TEE attestation of delivery)? If yes, Strale's Reliability score advantage has closed.

2. Does Switchboard produce a forward-looking quality and reliability score an agent can read before the call to decide whether the capability is trustworthy enough for the task, with a methodology a buyer can audit? If yes, Strale's dual-score advantage has closed.

3. Does Switchboard generate a structural execution audit trail of every call as a customer-visible product? If yes, Strale's audit trail advantage has closed.

If any one of the three closes, update Competitive Landscape Section 6 within one revision cycle and escalate the closing of the structural distance as a strategic signal rather than a routine update. If all three close, Switchboard becomes a direct structural competitor and triggers a full strategic review of Strale's x402 positioning.

The commitment to this recurring check exists in three places for resilience: Competitive Landscape Section 6, Competitive Landscape page footer, and DEC-20260406-E. This To-do entry is the operational anchor that makes the commitment actionable rather than aspirational.

After each check, update the Last reviewed date on this entry, add a one-line note in the Notes field describing what was found, and re-set Status to Next up for the following cycle.
